prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with tg.start_soon/tg.start but the caller proceeds to yield the streams before post_writer has actually entered its stream context managers and is ready to consume from write_stream_reader, so early writes can be missed. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, requiring the caller to use `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` and await the ready signal before yielding. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json and add a helper to decide when to skip JSON pre-parsing for union annotations, but #3056's helper (_is_optional_str) is scoped to str|None and explicitly unwraps Annotated[...] first via a dedicated _unwrap_annotated() step. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so it does not fix the common real-world case of `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (a documented optional string param) - that arg is not `is` any member of _SIMPLE_TYPES, so pre-parsing still runs and the corruption bug persists for annotated params. #2032 also silently changes behavior for other simple-type unions it wasn't scoped to fix (str|int, str|bool, str|float), a broader and less-justified change than the narrowly-targeted, documented fix in #3056.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both rewrite RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py, replacing the old unconditional 'send an error response to indicate cancellation' code with spec-compliant cancellation handling. #2493 simply deletes the error-response send (and updates a now-stale comment/log line in server.py, with no functional change there since the code path already returned early). #2514 touches the same method but goes further: it imports CancelledNotificationParams to actually send a notifications/cancelled message for the locally-initiated cases (request timeout, caller-side cancellation), and removes the '# pragma: no cover' marker on the _entered guard, indicating new test coverage was added for that branch. #2493's approach leaves the peer with no signal at all when the local side times out or cancels a request it's handling, whereas #2514 covers that gap. members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with tg.start_soon/tg.start but the caller proceeds to yield the streams before post_writer has actually entered its stream context managers and is ready to consume from write_stream_reader, so early writes can be missed. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, requiring the caller to use `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` and await the ready signal before yielding.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json and add a helper to decide when to skip JSON pre-parsing for union annotations, but #3056's helper (_is_optional_str) is scoped to str|None and explicitly unwraps Annotated[...] first via a dedicated _unwrap_annotated() step. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so it does not fix the common real-world case of `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (a documented optional string param) - that arg is not `is` any member of _SIMPLE_TYPES, so pre-parsing still runs and the corruption bug persists for annotated params. #2032 also silently changes behavior for other simple-type unions it wasn't scoped to fix (str|int, str|bool, str|float), a broader and less-justified change than the narrowly-targeted, documented fix in #3056.

clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes this at the shared dispatch level: it extends the existing _restore_mcp_error()/from_error_data()/from_error() reconstruction path so it works for every MCPError subclass generically, with UrlElicitationRequiredError special-cased inside that one function, and it un-marks the `data` property as no-cover, indicating the round-trip is now exercised by a test. #2555 instead adds a bespoke `__reduce__` directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError that bypasses the shared dispatcher entirely. Since Python always calls the most-derived `__reduce__`, merging both would make #2478's `if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError` branch inside _restore_mcp_error permanently unreachable for that class — dead code. #2478's fix also generalizes to any other current/future MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor, whereas #2555 only covers this one subclass, so #2478 is the more complete fix to build on; #2555's test additions (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py) should be ported over if not already covered.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both rewrite RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py, replacing the old unconditional 'send an error response to indicate cancellation' code with spec-compliant cancellation handling. #2493 simply deletes the error-response send (and updates a now-stale comment/log line in server.py, with no functional change there since the code path already returned early). #2514 touches the same method but goes further: it imports CancelledNotificationParams to actually send a notifications/cancelled message for the locally-initiated cases (request timeout, caller-side cancellation), and removes the '# pragma: no cover' marker on the _entered guard, indicating new test coverage was added for that branch. #2493's approach leaves the peer with no signal at all when the local side times out or cancels a request it's handling, whereas #2514 covers that gap. Both edit the identical lines at the tail of cancel(), so they cannot both be merged without conflict.
